proposals: The Central Pollution Control Board should publish a compliance summary of plastic EPR annual returns filed after the 19 January 2026 amendment, by producer category, showing targets met and shortfalls, so the effect of removing End-of-Life certificates can be measured rather than assumed.

The Central Pollution Control Board should notify the verification guidelines the amendment requires within its six-month window and publish a list of registered environment auditors, so recycled-content and reuse targets are checked by named auditors under published rules.

The Central Pollution Control Board should publish quarterly figures for black mass produced by registered battery recyclers, and how much was refined in India, sold on or exported, so the market the CSE brief calls a black hole becomes visible in official data.

The Central Pollution Control Board should publish, by battery category, the tonnes registered recyclers actually received and processed against producers' EPR obligations each year, so the reverse-logistics gap — recyclers unable to obtain the batteries their certificates assume — is quantified.

The Ministry of Mines should report how much of the ₹1,500 crore National Critical Mineral Mission recycling incentive has been sanctioned and disbursed, to which recyclers, so it is clear whether the support is reaching the battery-recycling ecosystem or remains an approved allocation.
